t: A small low-power board with long-range LoRa radio and Bluetooth.
steps: Buy the board from SparkFun or DigiKey, plus a wide-band antenna and a LiPo battery.
Attach the antenna to the u.FL jack before you power the radio.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the SparkFun Apollo3 Boards package version 2.0.5 or later.
Install the CH340 USB driver on computers that need it.
Upload the Blink example and watch the blue LED on pin 18.
Install SparkFun's modified RadioLib library from the hookup guide.
Set your region in the settings file for areas outside the US.
Try the LoRaWAN example and send your first message to The Things Network.
meta: Open Board. From $54.95. A few stores.
